intent_en: To demonstrate that test-optional college admissions policies are associated with higher average student test scores and increased application volumes compared to test-required policies, thereby enhancing institutional selectivity.
previous_intent: To illustrate that test-optional colleges generally exhibit higher average SAT scores and increased application volumes compared to test-required colleges from 1992 to 2010.
narration_support: it definitely helps strengthen other metrics like acceptance rate, which makes schools look more selective.
chart_support: Side-by-side line charts comparing Average SAT scores and total Applications for test-optional versus test-required colleges from 1992 to 2010, showing test-optional institutions consistently achieving higher values in both categories.
evidence_note: The narration mentions strengthening metrics like acceptance rate to increase selectivity, while the chart explicitly visualizes the underlying drivers: higher average SAT scores and more applicants for test-optional schools (blue lines) compared to test-required schools (grey lines).
